events.text: This again. The smell of frying dough, the cart with the cracked wheel, the knife-grinder singing the same wrong words to the same old song. You are six years old and you have lived this morning before. In a moment a horse will bolt down this street, and a child in a red coat will be standing in the road.

choices.text: Stand where you stood last time, and let it happen

effects.log: You stand where you stood before. The horse bolts, the cart overturns, the street shouts. Everything happens exactly as it did. It is strange how much that steadies you.

choices.text: Pull the child in the red coat out of the road

effects.log: You run before anyone else has heard the hooves, and pull the child in the red coat into a doorway. The horse goes by like thunder. The whole street talks about the little one who knew.

choices.text: Wait by the knife-grinder for the purse that falls

effects.log: When the horse goes by, a merchant drops his purse in the scramble and never looks back. You knew it would be there. 30 taels, the first silver of this life.

choices.text: The red-inked page says: watch the rooftops

effects.log: You watch the rooftops, as the Guide says, and see what you never saw before: a figure in grey running along the ridge tiles, light as smoke, as if the roofs were a road. Someone in this town knows lightness arts.

events.text: This again. The sky is clear at breakfast, and nobody believes you about the rain. You are six years old, and you have lived this day before: the storm at noon, the river rising, the old footbridge to the temple going in the afternoon with three people on it.

choices.text: Do as you did last time, and stay indoors

effects.log: You stay in and listen to the storm. In the afternoon the shouting starts down by the river, the same as before. You knew it would. Knowing is a heavy thing for a child to carry.

choices.text: Sit on the bridge steps and refuse to let anyone cross

effects.log: You sit on the bridge steps in the rain and scream at anyone who tries to cross. They call you a strange child. At three the bridge goes into the river, empty. Nobody calls you strange after that.

choices.text: Shelter early in the temple, by the old monk's shelf

effects.log: You are at the temple before the first drop falls. The old monk lets you sit by his shelf of sutras all afternoon. Last time you never learned to read until you were ten. This time you start today.

choices.text: The red-inked page says: the river shows what it hides

effects.log: When the water falls back, the Guide's page is right: an old iron box lies in the mud below the broken bridge, and nobody else has seen it. 25 taels, green with age.

events.text: This again. At noon a wandering master will walk into the village, dusty to the knees, and ask for water at the well. You are six years old. The first time you lived this day, you hid behind the well and watched. Every time since, you have known exactly what the master is looking for.

choices.text: Hide behind the well, as you did the first time

effects.log: You hide behind the well and watch the master drink, and go, the same as ever. You could have stood up. You wanted to see if anything would change on its own. Nothing does.

choices.text: Draw the water before the master asks

effects.log: You have the bucket up before the master reaches the well. The master drinks, looks at you a long time, and shows you how to stand so the weight goes into the ground. You practise it every day after.

choices.text: Say the first line of the method you will learn years from now

effects.log: You say the first line of a breathing method you will not be taught for ten years. The master goes very still, then laughs, and corrects your breathing on the second word. It is the right correction.

choices.text: The red-inked page says: the master has a name

effects.log: You say the name the Guide wrote in red. The master stares, then bows to a child of six, and says only "Then we will meet again." Something about the jianghu has noticed you already.

events.text: This again. The lantern festival: paper fish on strings, a juggler who drops the third ball, a fortune teller under the willow who will tell you, as she always does, that you have an old soul. You are six years old, and you have lived this night before.

choices.text: Let the night happen the way it always does

effects.log: You watch the juggler drop the third ball and laugh exactly where you laughed before. The fortune teller says you have an old soul. You say, "I know," and she does not know what to make of you.

choices.text: Catch the juggler's third ball before it falls

effects.log: You are under the third ball before it slips, and catch it. The crowd roars. The juggler, delighted, makes you part of the act for the rest of the night. Half the town knows your name by morning.

choices.text: Tell the fortune teller her own fortune

effects.log: You sit down under the willow and tell the fortune teller what happens to her next year, as you remember it. She goes pale, then presses a charm into your hand for luck. She was not going to give it to anyone.

choices.text: The red-inked page says: follow the blue lantern

effects.log: You follow the one blue lantern through the crowd, as the Guide says, to a stall nobody else sees, where an old man presses a lucky coin and 20 taels into your hand and says you dropped them. You did not.
